subject: QBR: runway thermometer & infra unit-econ collateral
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-21T16:12:00Z
Subject: QBR: runway thermometer & infra unit-econ collateral

Team —

We need a compact "runway thermometer" artifact for the upcoming QBR that ties together: committed GPU capacity, short-term demand signal (next 90 days), utilization delta, and the unit-economic impact from batching / caching levers. Leadership wants a single-sided PDF we can drop into the exec deck and a 2-slide backup that shows assumptions and sensitivity bands.

Ask (due EOD Monday, 72h):
- One-page thermometer: current committed GPUs, committed v. buffer, expected demand curve (conservative/likely/optimistic), and a runway indicator in days.
- Unit-econ snapshot: $/token (hosted) & $/GPU-hour (reserved), current observed util, and delta from enabling aggressive batching and cross-request KV caching.
- Quick risk callouts: big customers we expect to expand (naming ok), procurement timelines for reserved additions, and any SLA exceptions we might need to request.

Irene — can you include the forecast delta if Acme AI flips on their bulk expansion (rough magnitude, procurement lead time)? Jonas — please sanity-check the util assumptions and the bandwidth implications for Dedicated vs Hosted routing.

I attached a skeleton workbook (qbr_runway_model_v2.xlsx) with two tabs: inputs + sim. Use it as you like.

We will pre-brief execs Tues AM; Markus

--
Markus Klein
VP, Infrastructure & Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-21T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: QBR: runway thermometer & infra unit-econ collateral

Thanks Markus — I can take lead on the one-pager and the 2-slide backup. Quick notes on deliverables and approach:

- Thermometer will show three scenarios (base/peaky/expansion) with a small table below showing key levers (batch size, cache hit%, reserved v. spot mix).
- Unit-econ: I will compute marginal $/token across hosted vs reserved using our cost model and current utilization; I will present impact as a % reduction rather than absolute when the math gets noisy.
- I will include a short appendix row for the cost of enabling aggressive batching (latency/P95 impact + engineering risk).

Question: do you want Dedicated-reserved forecast included in the public deck, or only in the backup? My inclination is to keep capacity commitments in backup and show only runway % and days on the public slide.

Attaching my working workbook now. [attachment: qbr_runway_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Lauren
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-22T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: QBR: runway thermometer & infra unit-econ collateral

Forwarding my quick sims and a note on Acme — see CSV attached.

On the Acme expansion: procurement pinged us last week that they will pilot a "priority tier" for a pool of 200 reserved GPUs, start date target Dec 1. Procurement lead time looks like 6–8 weeks if they sign the SOW this month. Impact to runway: worst-case shortfall of ~35 GPU-hours/day if we don't provision buffer (we see ~72% util today on affected pools).

Cache/batching sims summary (from attached):
- 10% cache hit increase reduces token spend by ~8% on the workload sample (non-linear due to prefix reuse).
- Increasing batch windows to 120ms increases P95 by ~140ms on long prompts; net cost saves ~11% at scale but introduces risk for interactive flows.

[attachment: cache_batching_sim.csv (CSV export - sim runs)]

I flagged JIRA-OPS-1287 for a spot-to-reserved runway request and added supporting numbers.

Irene
Sr Manager, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-24T18:04:00Z
Subject: Re: QBR: runway thermometer & infra unit-econ collateral

Great work — thanks. Quick decisions and next steps: 

- Lauren: move the committed/reserved numbers to the backup slide only; public slide shows runway % and days (agreed).
- Irene: please open procurement escalation for Acme (JIRA-OPS-1287); lean on CloudMarketplace channel if needed to speed reserved availability.
- Jonas: we'll adopt the conservative util band for the public slide; include optimistic bucket in backup.

Schedule: 30-min pre-brief Tues 09:00 PT (invite incoming). Final slides to me by Mon EOD so I can assemble the exec deck Tue morning.

Also: we've got a pending SLA exception ask for Acme's priority lane; I've drafted a short exception we can submit with the SOW — attaching for comments. [attachment: SLA_exception_draft.docx]

Please redact any customer-identifying details from the public slide; the backup can be explicit.

Thanks — marking this closed for the thread, will re-open on any material changes.
